target_customer: Urban consumers buying and selling used furniture, initially in the New York tri-state area
problem: Selling used furniture on Craigslist meant scams, hard pickup logistics and awkward meetups; AptDeco manages payment, pickup and delivery.
business_model: Marketplace take rate (14 to 19 percent at launch) plus delivery fees
product_category: Managed peer to peer used furniture marketplace

founders.name: Reham Fagiri
founders.background_notes: Background not found in an opened source.

founders.name: Kalam Dennis
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page as kalam dennis and named a co-founder by TechCrunch (2014-02-21).

competitors.name: Chairish
competitors.what: Online marketplace for used furniture and decor

competitors.name: Viyet
competitors.what: Online consignment marketplace for designer furniture
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch as a rival with higher fees

technical_complexity.rationale: Marketplace software is standard; the difficulty is operations, delivery logistics and payments.

defensibility.rationale: Local supply and delivery operations helped but rivals and general marketplaces could copy the model.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Move Loot, a YC furniture resale rival, shut down in June 2016 and AptDeco said it had discussed an acquisition; AptDeco continued.

market_need_then: AptDeco's story cites scams and delivery problems on Craigslist and Facebook Marketplace as the pain, and TechCrunch noted the fee gap to Chairish.

branding.community_and_virality: A WeFunder community raise in 2025 suggests customer following but this was not confirmed in a brand source.

brand_strength.rationale: Name hints at apartment decor and became known in New York resale; little brand specific evidence found.

outcome_analysis: AptDeco joined YC in Winter 2014 with a managed used furniture marketplace in New York, outlasted peer Move Loot which shut in 2016, and expanded nationwide. Aggregators show multiple seed rounds, debt and a 2025 crowd raise totaling roughly $16M to $27M, so it looks like a durable but capital hungry marketplace; none of this is confirmed by primary sources.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights lists $16.1M over 11 rounds including a $5.84M convertible note via WeFunder in May 2025 and $6.15M debt in March 2023; Standout lists $26.8M; a Forbes headline cited by 645 Ventures says more than $20M in July 2025. 645 Ventures, SV Angel, Y Combinator, Liquid 2 and FJ Labs are listed as investors by aggregators. No press release for any round was found, so no rounds are recorded. The AptDeco about page returned no content. The Move Loot detail comes from a search summary of a TechCrunch article of June 2016. The site is active with open roles. Audit update: 2023-03 round of 6.15M comes from AlleyWatch (funding report of 2023-03-21), which cites a recent SEC filing (not opened) with a 7M total offering and four unnamed investors; stage is other because the instrument is not stated (CB Insights calls it debt). The 2025-05 note of 5.84M (5,839,052 per Kingscrowd) is a convertible note with a 40M cap tied to Wefunder; Kingscrowd and CB Insights are both aggregators, so it rests on database reporting, and the Wefunder campaign itself had a 618K maximum per P2P Market Data (July 2024 to April 2025), so the 5.84M may include other money; investors are recorded only as Wefunder crowd. Not recorded for lack of a source: a 2016-08 round of 3.6M (no source found; search hits were other companies such as Apptentive and Abodo) and a 2024-07 crowdfunding of about 5M (the only 5M figure found sits beside an unrelated land-and-permits listing, and the 2024 Wefunder offering was 50K to 618K, so it is not attributed). Kingscrowd also lists a 2023 note near 5.4M while P2P Market Data shows 401,868 raised on Wefunder by 2023-04-30; these conflict and are not recorded. Totals differ widely by database: 16.1M (CB Insights), 26.8M (PitchBook), 26.29M (Caplight).
